metadata.source: Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 - Incident Patterns for Scenario Understanding
metadata.purpose: Map real-life scenarios to WLPA sections, offences, and procedures

dead_animal.name: Dead Animal Found
dead_animal.description: Finding a dead wild animal (natural causes, poaching, accident, electrocution, etc.)
scenarios: Dead schedule I animal on railway track/road
Dead bird (vulture, bustard) near power lines
practicalSteps: Do NOT touch/move the carcass
Inform nearest Forest Department office immediately
Note location (GPS if possible), date, time
Take photos from distance (don't disturb evidence)
Wait for Forest Dept / authorized officer
If poaching suspected: inform police/WCCB

poaching.name: Poaching / Illegal Hunting
poaching.description: Illegal killing, trapping, poisoning of wild animals
practicalSteps: Report immediately to Forest Dept / Police / WCCB
Do not confront poachers - safety first
Note: vehicle numbers, descriptions, GPS location
Preserve evidence: don't touch traps/snares/weapons
Forest officers can arrest without warrant (Section 50)
Presumptions under Section 57 favor prosecution

illegal_trade.name: Illegal Wildlife Trade
illegal_trade.description: Possession, sale, transport, smuggling of wildlife parts/products
practicalSteps: Report to Forest Dept / WCCB / Customs / Police
Do not buy/handle suspected illegal wildlife products
Online trade: report to platform + enforcement agencies
Check for ownership certificate (Section 42) before any purchase
CITES permits mandatory for international trade (Schedule IV)
Scheduled specimens (Schedule IV) - registration required (Section 49M)

human_wildlife_conflict.name: Human-Wildlife Conflict
human_wildlife_conflict.description: Crop damage, livestock depredation, human injury/death, property damage by wildlife
practicalSteps: Do NOT kill/injure animal - illegal without permit
Contact Forest Dept immediately for conflict situations
Apply for ex-gratia compensation from State Govt
Preventive measures: fencing, early warning, crop insurance
Section 11 permit ONLY from CWLW for dangerous animals
Tiger reserves: buffer zone coexistence measures (Section 38V)
Community reserves for community-based management (Section 36C)

plant_destruction.name: Protected Plant Destruction
plant_destruction.description: Illegal collection, uprooting, trade of Schedule VI plants
practicalSteps: Do not collect plants from forests/protected areas
Check if plant is Schedule VI before any collection
Cultivation/dealing requires licence from CWLW
Report illegal plant trade to Forest Dept
CITES permits for international plant trade (Schedule IV)

nest_disturbance.name: Nest/Breeding Site Disturbance
nest_disturbance.description: Disturbance of nesting sites, breeding colonies, eggs, chicks
practicalSteps: Do NOT disturb nests, eggs, chicks - it's hunting under Section 9
Report nest disturbance to Forest Dept
Tree cutting: check for nests first, avoid breeding season
Turtle nesting beaches: no lights, no vehicles, no disturbance
Photography: maintain distance, no flash at nests
Community protection of nesting sites encouraged

illegal_possession.name: Illegal Possession of Wildlife/Parts
illegal_possession.description: Possessing wild animals, parts, products without legal authority
scenarios: Keeping parrot/turtle as pet without certificate
Possessing tiger claw/leopard tooth as talisman
practicalSteps: Declare ALL wildlife items within 30 days (Section 40)
Apply for ownership certificate (Section 42)
Schedule IV (CITES) living animals: register with Management Authority (Section 49M)
Voluntary surrender option: Section 42A (no compensation)
Inherited items: declare and get certificate
Burden of proof on YOU to show legal possession (Section 57)

animal_attack.name: Wild Animal Attack on Human
animal_attack.description: Wild animal injuring or killing a person

immediate: 11 - CWLW can permit hunting if dangerous to human life

practicalSteps: Immediate medical attention for victim
Inform Forest Dept / Police immediately
CWLW can issue Section 11 permit for dangerous animal
Do NOT take matters into own hands - illegal hunting
Apply for ex-gratia compensation from State Govt
Forest Dept will assess: problem animal vs chance encounter
Capture/tranquilize by authorized team only

vehicle_seizure.name: Vehicle Used in Wildlife Offence
vehicle_seizure.description: Vehicle/vessel seized for transporting wildlife contraband or used in poaching
scenarios: Boat used for illegal fishing/turtle poaching
practicalSteps: Authorized officers can seize vehicle on suspicion
Vehicle produced before Magistrate
Confiscation if offence proved
Owner can claim if not involved (burden on owner)
2022: More officers authorized (Management Authority, customs, coast guard)
